analyticalMisses.summary: Toronto 5+ runs at 59%: a defensible family and rung, but the implied scoring distribution was too confident for the price paid. Defensible-but-overconfident, not a process failure.
Milwaukee 5+ runs at 44% lacked the coherent starter + bullpen + lineup mechanism the winning team-total positions had. Scanning every rung does not mean betting every rung.
Sandy Alcantara 19+ outs YES at 39% rested on a workload thesis that was not durably established. A high outs threshold needs a documented role expectation, not an assumption.

analyticalWins.summary: Andrew Painter 16+ outs NO at 44% was the model structural outs bet: an explicit, documented workload/role constraint plus a severe pitch-count matchup, not a recent-innings extrapolation. This is the template pitcher-outs unders must meet.

Houston F5 YES at 39% was a correctly-sized secondary expression of the same HOU/PHI thesis ($8 against Painter's $12, one $20 budget). Related but non-identical cash paths, and the three-way tie risk was priced into the stake, not ignored.
Cincinnati 4+ runs NO at 64% came from scanning every team-total rung rather than defaulting to the headline number, with a coherent starter + bullpen + lineup suppression mechanism behind it.
Seattle F5 NO at ~55% is protected F5 done correctly: the tie branch is bought at a price that still pays meaningfully. Contrast with PIT F5 NO at ~65% the same night.
TB/ATL first 5 innings over 4.5 at 51% had a real two-sided scoring mechanism rather than a recent-scoring extrapolation.
Ty France 1+ hits at 62% is the low-threshold, high-floor end of the hitter board -- a defensible small position, not a lottery rung.

processErrors.summary: Jacob Misiorowski 18+ outs NO is a PROCESS FAILURE, not a bad result. His elite strikeout/whiff/xFIP profile and normal workload made an under-outs recommendation insufficiently justified. Pitcher-outs unders require a STRUCTURAL innings-suppression mechanism (pitch/innings cap, injury return, opener/bulk role, demonstrably short leash, severe pitch-count matchup, or another durable workload constraint). Variance is not a workload edge.

Pittsburgh F5 NO at 64.9% is a PROCESS FAILURE on price discipline, not on the idea. Protected F5 is not banned -- but above roughly 60-65% the payout no longer compensates the variance, and this was also a poor handicap on the merits. Compare SEA F5 NO at ~55% the same night.
St. Louis moneyline at 51% was manufactured largely out of recent offensive form. Recent form must not manufacture a large edge on a coin-flip-priced market. Should have passed.
MIN/DET first 5 innings over 4.5 at 49% for $25 leaned on recent scoring and recent FIP rather than a durable mechanism, and it was the second-largest stake of the day. Too speculative for the size.

proposedInvestigations.summary: Gate every pitcher-outs UNDER behind an explicit, named structural innings-suppression mechanism. Reject the recommendation when the only support is recent short or volatile innings.
Apply a price ceiling to protected F5 (side NO): above roughly 60-65%, require exceptional evidence before the position is allowed.
Cap how much recent offensive form / recent FIP may contribute to a stated edge, so recent form cannot manufacture a large edge on a near-coin-flip price.
Keep scanning every game and every family/rung, and verify that the widening candidate universe never lowers the betting threshold.

periodCovered.note: Period-level findings for the 2026-09-08..2026-09-10 user-confirmed manual MLB wager block. Recorded on each date's postmortem so every date's structured record stands alone.

periodKeyFindings.summary: Every game and every available Kalshi family/rung should be considered. A larger candidate universe must NOT lower the betting threshold.
periodKeyFindings.title: Full-universe scan remains required

periodKeyFindings.summary: Do not bet pitcher-outs unders primarily because recent innings have been short or volatile. Require a structural innings-suppression mechanism: a documented pitch/innings cap, injury return, opener/bulk role, demonstrably short managerial leash, severe pitch-count matchup, or another durable workload constraint. Variance is not a workload edge.
periodKeyFindings.title: Pitcher-outs UNDER rule

periodKeyFindings.summary: Pregame profile: 27.6% K, 32% whiff, 3.63 xERA, 3.82 xFIP, 5.4 IP/start, 3.29 recent FIP. The wager over-weighted his recent variable innings and ignored the substantial dominant-start branch. Jared Jones 16+ NO is graded a BAD RECOMMENDATION, not merely a bad result.
periodKeyFindings.title: Jared Jones was a process failure

periodKeyFindings.summary: His elite strikeout/whiff/xFIP profile and normal workload made the under-outs recommendation insufficiently justified.
periodKeyFindings.title: Misiorowski outs-under was also a process failure

periodKeyFindings.summary: Painter 16+ NO and Wheeler 18+ YES both had explicit workload/role/matchup justification. Treat structural workload reasoning separately from speculative recent-IP reasoning.
periodKeyFindings.title: Structural outs bets performed differently

periodKeyFindings.summary: Successful NYY/KC/CIN positions had coherent starter + workload/TTO + bullpen + lineup scoring mechanisms. Do not overfit the 5-3 result, but continue scanning every rung.
periodKeyFindings.title: Team totals remain a priority market family

periodKeyFindings.summary: Yamamoto 8+ at 48% was one of the strongest bets in the period because K ability x expected batters faced/workload x opponent strikeout profile x price all aligned.
periodKeyFindings.title: Strikeout props deserve serious attention

periodKeyFindings.summary: Painter NO + HOU F5 = $12 + $8 = $20 combined: a well-sized split with related but non-identical cash paths. Jones NO + CWS 4+ = $50 + $48 = $98 combined: an unacceptable concentration around a weak shared thesis.
periodKeyFindings.title: Same-thesis splits are allowed but share one exposure budget

periodKeyFindings.summary: Yamamoto 8+ Ks + CIN 4+ NO totaled $70. The thesis was strong and both won, but 7% of a ~$1,000 bankroll is still elevated correlated exposure and must not become the normal template.
periodKeyFindings.title: Correlated winners do not excuse oversizing

periodKeyFindings.summary: Protected F5 is not banned. At ~55%, SEA F5 NO had a meaningful payout and a coherent tie-protection rationale. At ~65%, PIT F5 NO was an unattractive high-variance risk/reward profile and a poor handicap. Protected F5 above roughly 60-65% should require exceptional evidence.
periodKeyFindings.title: Protected F5 price discipline

periodKeyFindings.summary: Do not classify it as a process failure merely because it lost. The pregame starter-quality mismatch was meaningful.
periodKeyFindings.title: BOS F5 is a good-process loss

periodKeyFindings.summary: Do not promote it retrospectively simply because it cashed.
periodKeyFindings.title: TB-ATL full-game Over 7.5 was a B-tier winner

periodKeyFindings.summary: STL ML and MIN-DET F5 Over are examples where recent offense/recent FIP was weighted too heavily.
periodKeyFindings.title: Recent form must not manufacture large edges

periodKeyFindings.summary: Winning does not validate oversizing. A secondary expression recommended for small exposure must not silently become a large independent position.
periodKeyFindings.title: Sizing discipline

periodKeyFindings.summary: The postmortem must explicitly separate good process/win, good process/loss, weak process/win, and weak process/loss.
periodKeyFindings.title: Outcome vs process
